rules.observation: Persistent mixed-work queues and long first-forward waits coexist with many fast requests; client TTFT tails are much longer than connection/send overhead.
rules.diagnosis: Admission ordering may repeatedly favor inexpensive uncached work. Shortest-prefill-first uses age only as a tie-breaker; initial queue waits are distinct from later chunk execution and router delay.
alternatives: Cadence, token/capacity gates or cache readiness can delay admission independent of sorting.
An increase in observed long waits can mean old backlog is finally being admitted; still-waiting requests remain censored.
Closed-loop trajectory progress and cache locality change with policy; total input length is not uncached work.

Shortest-prefill-first uniquely reserves continuation budget for shorter waiting requests and gates the chunk-slot event. HRRN removes that reservation, so a single policy flag changes more than sorting; absent chunk-slot events under HRRN are expected producer semantics.
rules.check: Use source-defined queue histogram bucket/count/sum deltas by rank and observation time, plus finalized client request-start strata and cancellations. The sampled shortest_uncached log describes the first sorted request, not the oldest. Verify HRRN processed-token arrival/accounting path before proposing it. HRRN age advances with processed prefill tokens, not wall time; inspect queue-entry/requeue snapshots. Record continuation-reservation changes and event producer conditions before comparison. Distinguish current queue-episode perf_counter age from submitted-token age and actual readiness: sorting precedes budget/prefetch/staging checks. Unified reentry resets both age origins. HRRN and SPF estimate output-bearing work differently; establish its incidence before using that difference to explain performance. Verify tuning_policy_config and sample coverage by rank. Read queue snapshots, visit outcomes and continuation separately; candidates not visited have unknown readiness, and a selected head is not necessarily admitted. Compare paired age/work within the same record. Snapshot counts are not request arrival rates or wait seconds. Configured HRRN falls back to FCFS above128waiting requests. Check effective_policy and queue_snapshot_available before interpreting sort-derived fields; candidate work retains the configured-policy estimate. Source fallback alone does not establish R7 incidence.
rules.action: Validate the new sampled diagnostics on R6/SPF first. Old queued work while the selected head repeatedly has smaller estimated work motivates a policy/reservation test, but eligibility is unproven. Old visited candidates reporting prefetch/staging pending motivate cache-readiness investigation. Repeated budget stops plus observed continuation reservation/admission motivate budget or reservation changes after memory validation. Use complete full-run throughput, tails and cancellations to choose among these actions; no automatic action from one sample.

rules.observation: GPU management snapshots show very little free memory, possibly without corresponding KV admission failures.
rules.diagnosis: Physical usage is not decomposed by logical KV utilization or the configured static fraction. Live tensors, reserved allocator blocks, graph/private pools and external symmetric buffers are competing contributors.
alternatives: A large reserved footprint may coexist with reusable blocks; reserved minus allocated is not guaranteed reclaimable.
PyTorch stats may exclude custom/private pools and external library allocations.
Request shape, startup history and lazy capture differ across ranks and runs.
rules.check: Retain timestamped GPU samples and resolved pool capacities. On a later validated deployment, enable the optional native-allocator snapshot and inspect allocated/reserved/active bytes plus same-process retry/OOM counter deltas. Unsupported, missing and error statuses remain unknown. Use actual buffer-creation receipts for external allocation provenance. Size external buffers with the resolved aligned cap. Retire earlier unaligned API estimates as actual allocation or headroom evidence; no corrected baseline delta was measured by this probe.
rules.action: Keep an active benchmark unchanged. If an actual allocation failure occurs, preserve it and choose one memory-headroom intervention for a fresh trial. When memory provenance is ambiguous, validate and enable bounded allocator/buffer receipts in a separate instrumentation trial before attributing low free memory to a particular config. Never flush caches or reset peaks in a live comparison to manufacture headroom.
rules.expected: Allocator snapshots distinguish supported native allocator counters from unknown external/pool contributions; a later headroom intervention should reduce actual allocation failures without an unacceptable capacity/throughput loss.
rules.reject_if: Snapshot coverage/backend is unknown, observation changes behavior materially, or only a reserved-memory subtraction supports the claimed cause.

rules.observation: Startup stops before weight loading; some ranks emit PIL fallback but another remains in an optional cargo version subprocess.
rules.diagnosis: The optional auto image-backend probe can invoke Rustup toolchain setup. Other ranks may wait for the blocked rank even on a text-only workload.
alternatives: Distributed initialization, weight I/O, compilation, or loader errors can also leave quiet logs; confirm the exact child and source interval.
rules.check: Inspect actual per-rank milestones and the owned cargo child command, parent and executable. Missing fallback warning is unknown, not success. No throughput diagnosis follows from this startup delay.
rules.action: On the next fresh text-only deployment, explicitly select --image-processor-backend pil to reproduce the previously observed fallback; verify parser/resolved backend. Do not change a running config. A pre-traffic recovery may terminate only a positively identified stalled optional child to exercise existing fallback, with the intervention recorded.
rules.expected: The optional Rust image probe is bypassed and startup reaches weight loading without waiting for toolchain installation. No throughput gain is claimed.
rules.reject_if: The stall is elsewhere, PIL is rejected, effective backend differs, or image-input semantics are required and have not been validated.
rules.status: R8b pre-traffic recovery verified. Explicit PIL launch is source-supported but not yet deployed or runtime-verified.
runtime_evidence: R8b rank2 waited in cargo --version --verbose via /root/.cargo/bin/rustup. Exact verified child was terminated before traffic at08:13:43UTC; rank2 emitted PIL fallback and all ranks reached weight loading at08:13:45. Historical R6/R7 logs also report PIL fallback.

policy.units: Keep rank/process labels; encounter counts are not unique requests, wait seconds or fallback percentages.
policy.window: First characterize the full canonical AgentX hour. Read changing workload/cache regimes with graph evidence throughout; consistent early windows do not establish the whole replay.
policy.early_stop: Full baseline/candidate runs continue through the requested measurement unless safety or invalidity requires stopping. Shorter diagnostic sections need an explicit, previously calibrated question.
policy.promotion: Use complete canonical runs, validity/accounting and refreshed latency/throughput frontiers for candidate ranking. Calibrate shorter sections against full-run outcomes later; retain missed regimes and counterexamples.
policy.unknown: Missing producers/events are unknown, not zero; add discriminating instrumentation when alternatives remain.
policy.finalization: Traffic completion, zero request errors and latency coverage do not by themselves establish a qualified result. Require complete canonical exports, validation and final accounting. Preserve artifacts durably from launch; distinguish external resource-guard termination from serving OOM.
